name: Crowned Ladies FR
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the block at the foot of the frame and every number in it are
the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this show
itself is one sentence long - it is set in Helvetica, in one magenta,
on the photograph itself with no card under it and with no highlight -
and everything below is that sentence.
The FR in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE is and the FR in Soccer Stories FR and Inkjection FR: it says which
of the brand's feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What
lands on the frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying,
put through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every
channel here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app
itself says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
One thing this pack checked that its English-feed siblings had no
reason to, and that the two DE feeds and Inkjection FR checked before
it. The Helvetica file carries 2012 codepoints and covers what French
actually needs - the acute and the grave, the circumflex and the
diaeresis on the vowels that take them, the cedilla, the o-e ligature
in both cases, the angle quotes French sets speech in and the curly
apostrophe it elides with - so a caption is drawn from the file rather
than from whatever the browser substitutes for a missing glyph, which
would be a different face at a width nothing measured. Worth stating
because a face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically
a face that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes
against a cmap.
A folder of its own rather than a second colourway of Hall of Femme,
for the reason oh-my-goal-news is a folder of its own: the person
picking a channel at the top of the app picks this one or that one and
never both, and these two do not merely disagree about colour - they
are set in different type, one of them has no card at all and one of
them has no highlight, which is as far as two packs under one heading
go.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Helvetica, in one magenta, straight onto the PHOTOGRAPH with no
card behind it, and every line of every caption is set the same way.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, where the block stands on the frame, the drag - is
the Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states what makes it
this show, and then states the two keys the missing card forces:
`shadow`, which has to come back, and `panel`, which has to be said out
loud to go away.
Helvetica is the plainest thing a caption here has been set in, and
that is the brand rather than a shortage of ideas. Its siblings pick a
face with a voice - a hairline, a hand, a serif, a condensed display
cut - and then spend a card or a halo making that voice survive a
photograph. This one picks the face that has been the neutral of signage
for seventy years, which is the one kind of type that can stand on an
unknown picture without an argument: even strokes at a single weight,
closed apertures, no thins for a photograph to eat. What it needs from
this pack is not rescuing but separation, and that is the shadow below.
Uppercased, inherited, for the reason every one of its neighbours is:
at 40px with twenty characters to a line the caption is three short
beats rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are set in.
It costs nothing here - Helvetica's capitals are the half of the face
the world knows it by.

_comment_color: A magenta, and it is the whole palette rather than the first of
several: this show is set in one colour. It is therefore also what
every frame is drawn in, since a frame stores no colour of its own
until it is given one and there is no swatch here to give it one
It is the loudest thing this heading has put on a photograph, and on
a channel with no card that is the point. A caption with no ground
under it is separated from the picture by two things only - its
colour and its shadow - and a colour that occurs in almost no
photograph is doing half of that work before the shadow is asked for
anything. Skin, hair, daylight, studio walls: none of them is this.
Which frame is the risky one follows from where the colour sits. Its
relative luminance is about 0.27, so it stands roughly six times
clear of a black and only three times clear of a white - a night
still holds it easily and a blown, sunlit one is where it thins out.
That is the still the shadow below is chosen for, and it is why the
_comment_colors: Absent, and that is the palette being stated rather than forgotten.
Hall of Femme, the pack this is cut from, offers rows of swatches
because its look IS the pairing - which of its colours is the card
and which is the type. This show has one colour and no card, so
there is no pairing to offer and nothing for a second button to be.
Left unstated rather than written as a list of one, which is the
answer Inkjection FR reached in the same position: a row of one
swatch is a control that cannot change anything - it draws the
colour already on screen, marked as chosen, and clicking it does
nothing a user can see. That is the one kind of control this panel
does not have anywhere (see the note on `alignable` in js/editor.js).
With no list the whole block of colour rows is hidden instead - see
editor.paletteOf, which hides a row whose colours have nothing to
recolour, and renderColorButtons, which drops the block when no row
Nothing counts these lists, so the day this show wants a second
colour it is one key in this file and the row appears.
_comment_shadow: An exception to the preset, and the first of the two keys the
missing card forces.
The preset states no shadow, and its reasoning is exact: there is a
solid slab under those letters in a colour the user picked, it
separates them from the photograph completely, and a shadow as well
would only smear the inside of the card. Take the card away and
every word of that stops being true - these letters are on a
photograph, with grain and edges and whatever was behind the subject
running through them.
A DARK shadow, which is the opposite of what Inkjection FR does with
the other cardless caption under this heading, and the two are the
same decision made about two different colours. That channel's navy
is nearly black, so a black shadow under it would be dark on dark
and it carries a white halo instead. This magenta sits in the middle
of the range and is in trouble at the light end rather than the dark
one (see `color` above): it is a bright still that swallows it, and
what a mid-tone letter needs on a bright ground is a dark edge.
The numbers are the skeleton's own (see BASE_TITLE_STYLE.shadow in
js/channels.js) rather than a fresh set invented here. They are what
every channel in this app that sets type on a photograph uses, which
is the same job this is; a pack with no reason of its own should not
carry a number it merely agrees with, and where it has to state one
anyway it should state the one already in use.
_comment_highlight: None. Every line of every caption on this channel is set the same
way, and the highlight buttons stand where they stand everywhere
else and go dead with a tooltip saying whose decision that was (see
editor.renderHlButtons). A brand whose lines are all one treatment
says so here rather than being given a highlight nobody could tell
apart from the type - see `highlight` in js/channels.js.
All three things a highlight could be are unavailable to this show,
and they run out in order. A change of CUT is what most of this
heading picks its words out with, and the app carries one cut of
Helvetica; asking for a second weight of it would be the browser
emboldening the one file there is, and a synthesised weight is
measured as well as drawn. A recolour needs a second colour, and
this show has one. And a box needs a fill, which would be a second
colour again - and a graphic in the one frame under this heading
whose whole design is type lying directly on the picture.
Written as null rather than left out, for the reason `panel` below
is: `use` merges the preset UNDER this pack (see `expand` in
js/channels.js), so the preset's word-scope colour highlight arrives
whatever this pack says about it. Null is how a pack cut from that
preset declines the feature.
There is no `colors.highlight` either - there is no palette here at
all - so nothing draws a swatch row for words that cannot be picked
out (see editor.paletteOf, which hides that row on a channel with no
highlight).
_comment_panel: None, and its absence is half of this channel's design. Written as
null rather than left out, which is the opposite of what
laugh-society-snapchat does and is right for the opposite reason:
that pack inherits nothing, so a key restating the skeleton's own
null would read as a slab somebody had switched off. This one takes
the Snapchat caption preset, and the preset states a card - its
shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow. Null here is what
removes it, and it has to be said out loud.
Why drop it. On Hall of Femme the card and the hairline are one
decision: a 200-weight face over an unknown photograph disappears,
and the slab is what makes that weight a choice rather than a risk.
Helvetica at 400 has no such problem, so a card under it would be a
fifth of the frame of flat colour spent on a difficulty this face
does not have - and it would cover the picture the captions exist to
There is no `colors.panel` either, so the swatch row that fills a
card on most of its siblings is not drawn at all rather than drawn

_comment_branding: No dark gradient, like every pack under this heading - and like
Conspiracy Central this is a channel where the usual reason does not
apply, because its siblings say the gradient has nothing to do when a
title is on a card rather than on the photograph, and this title IS on
the photograph.
It still has nothing to do. The backend's gradient is a SIDE gradient -
full height, never past half the width, peaking on whichever side the
title column is (reframe_engine.apply_dark_gradient) - because it was
drawn for a landscape thumbnail with a headline set beside the subject.
There is no title column on a captured still: the block lies across the
width of the frame, and darkening one half of forty pictures would shade
half of every caption and leave the other half exactly as it was.
No `scrim` either, which is the tool that WOULD reach across the foot of
the frame. Laugh Society throws one and sets white type on it, and that
pairing is what a scrim is for. Under a magenta the trade is worse than
it looks: the shade would buy this colour a little at the light end of
the range, where the dark shadow is already helping, and cost it at the
dark end, where the caption and the shade are the same kind of dark.
What holds this type off the photograph is its own drop shadow, one
letter at a time, which leaves all forty pictures whole.
